summary: FunnelEventService dispatcher + FunnelExecutionFactory cycle-break + project-scoped SubscriberService.findById. Architecture is sound: the factory removes any FunnelEventService->FunnelTriggerServiceImpl edge and has no engine edge, so the Task-5 StepExecutor->FunnelEventService edge cannot close a cycle (confirmed by IT context boot). Error-isolation, PII-safe logging, and the three backstops are correctly implemented. A few minor findings.

findings.finding: The volume rate-limit (depth>0) is consulted BEFORE the subscriber is resolved. An auto-enroll dispatch for a non-existent / foreign-project subscriberId still consumes one Redis token (INCR) before the no-subscriber no-op. Harmless (bounded per subscriberId, no PII), but it lets an attacker-influenced subscriberId burn rate-limit tokens it will never enroll under.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is for this task: the depth cap + fan-out ceiling still bound the cascade, the token key is per-subscriberId, and resolving the subscriber first would add a DB read on every depth-0 path (the common case) for marginal benefit. Documented; no change required.

findings.finding: Trigger-type comparison uses FunnelService.TRIGGER_KEYWORD / passes triggerType strings straight to the repo query. This matches the existing fire() convention (string triggerType) and reuses the canonical FunnelService constant, so no new magic literals are introduced.
findings.recommendation: No change — consistent with project convention.

findings.finding: LOG_EXECUTION_STARTED keeps the same string literal ('FUNNEL_FIRE_EXECUTION_STARTED') as the removed FunnelTriggerServiceImpl.LOG_FIRE_STARTED, so existing log-based alerts/greps still match. The log line now additionally includes enrollDepth, which is additive and safe.

notes: No critical or major findings. Cycle-break verified structurally (constructor of FunnelEventService injects FunnelExecutionFactory, not FunnelTriggerServiceImpl; factory injects only MongoTemplate + Clock). PII rule honoured (ids/codes only). Tests cover fan-out, all three backstops incl. Redis-down, keyword matching, error-isolation, and the anti-IDOR findById.
